tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[The house with two rooms is contractible] ↗ def:contractible ↗ def:mapping-cylinder \group Homotopy Theory

The house with two rooms is the 2-dimensional subspace $X\subset \R ^3$ formed from three horizontal annuli and vertical rectangular chamber and tunnel walls. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon $, a closed neighborhood $N(X)$ deformation retracts onto $X$ and is the mapping cylinder of its boundary surface mapping to $X$. \end{example}

Proof

\sketch A family of embeddings of $D^3$ into $\R ^3$, obtained by creating the two tunnels and chambers, identifies $N(X)$ with $D^3$. Hence $X\simeq N(X)\cong D^3\simeq \text{point}$. If $f_t$ contracts $N(X)$ to $x_0\in X$ and $r:N(X)\to X$ is a retraction, then $(r\circ f_t)|_X$ contracts $X$ to $x_0$.
